passage: L1.1: "Using the same dataset for training and testing the model is a textbook example of overfitting" (Results, 'Toward a solution: A taxonomy of data leakage', PMC10499856; as returned by the fetch tool).
faulty: Second-order polynomial regression (intercept, 10 linear terms, 10 squares, 45 pairwise products = 66 coefficients, standardised X, ordinary least squares) fitted on all 300 rows; Pearson correlation between its fitted values and y on the same 300 rows; holds iff >= 0.30.
fixed: 5-fold cross-validation, fold of row i = i mod 5; the same regression fitted on 240 rows predicts the 60 held-out rows; Pearson correlation between the pooled held-out predictions and y over all 300 rows; holds iff >= 0.30.
estimand: Faulty: the in-sample correlation between fitted and observed outcome (multiple correlation, positive even with no effect). Fixed: the correlation between out-of-sample predictions and observed outcomes for new runs.
model_family: Second-order polynomial regression by ordinary least squares (numpy lstsq), standardised readings. Chosen so the model capacity (66 coefficients) is a known function of the brief's 10 readings, and so it differs from the ridge model of B2A-01.
sizes_note: Source states none. 300 x 10 = 3,000 values: moderate-n regime where capacity (66 terms) is 22% of the samples; check is 5 lstsq fits (seconds). Dependence on sample size or feature count: not stated.
exploited_structure: Model capacity (number of fitted terms) that is a sizeable fraction of the number of samples, so fitted values track the observed outcomes of the rows they were fitted on.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: 65 non-constant polynomial terms / 300 samples is the brief's own size; set by the brief

notes: Guard: Pearson correlation undefined below 2 rows or with zero variance of predictions or y (None); non-finite returns None. Differs from B2A-01 in statistic (correlation vs R-squared), model and sample-size regime.
